questions.q: What does Mamet mean by telling a story through 'uninflected images'?
choices: Letting meaning arise from the juxtaposition of simple shots in the cut
questions.explain: Following Eisenstein's montage, each shot shows one plain thing, and the cut makes the meaning.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three questions in Mamet's memo to the writers of The Unit?
choices: What happens if they don't get it?
What does the character need, as opposed to want?
questions.explain: The want/need distinction belongs to other teachers. Mamet's third question is 'Why now?'

questions.q: A pilot's opening scene has two characters explaining the backstory of their unit to each other. Mamet would say…
choices: The audience won't tune in to watch information; let it emerge under pressure
Good: the audience needs information first
questions.explain: Exposition is the writer doing the audience's work for them.

questions.q: What test does the memo offer for a scene?
choices: Read it aloud to check rhythm
Imagine the characters can't speak: could it play as a silent film?
Check that it ends in disaster
questions.explain: If the scene only works through talk, it may be relying on dialogue instead of action.

questions.q: A scene is beautifully written but doesn't move the plot forward. According to the memo, it is…
questions.explain: Every scene must both advance the plot and work dramatically on its own.

questions.q: How does Mamet's view of character relate to Aristotle?
choices: He reverses Aristotle and puts character first
Like Aristotle, he ranks action above character: character is what people habitually do
He thinks character is revealed through backstory
questions.explain: An audience knows people only by their actions toward a goal.

choices: A scene that could happen any time has no urgency
questions.explain: Urgency comes from a reason this scene must happen today.

ideas: The director should tell the story through the cut, juxtaposing simple shots that each do one plain thing.
Every scene should answer who wants what, what happens if they don't get it, and why now.
Audiences won't sit still for information; if a scene couldn't play as a silent film, it's leaning on talk.
There is no character apart from habitual action.
